detailed_rationale:
JSLL is Jeena Sikho Lifecare Ltd, an Ayurvedic healthcare chain operating 119 active centres (61 hospitals plus 58 clinics/day-care centres) across 23 states and over 100 cities/towns, with about 2,300 operational beds and 592 certified Ayurveda doctors. This is a genuine multi-location rollout story, not a single-asset business: FY26 (year ended March 2026) revenue rose to Rs 801 crore from Rs 469 crore a year earlier (+71%), with net profit surging from Rs 80 crore to Rs 222 crore (+178%), an operating margin around 44%, and return ratios that are exceptional for a healthcare-services business (ROCE 64.1%, ROE 61.3%). Debtor days improved from 49 to 32, a genuine working-capital-quality improvement rather than just an income-statement story, and borrowings remain modest (Rs 127 crore) relative to the scale of the business.

The growth-quality check here comes out clean: this is a real, geographically-broad rollout (23 states, 100+ towns) rather than one or two centres distorting a small base, and profit grew faster than revenue on improving working capital, which is the opposite of an earnings-quality red flag. The company continues to invest in expansion (a new client-support centre in Noida, a new 60+ bed hospital planned in Kalyani, West Bengal by October 2026, and new Ayurvedic product launches), suggesting the growth algorithm is still being fed rather than harvested. The main caveats are that trailing growth of 70%+ cannot mechanically continue forever as the base of 119 centres scales further, and the stock's rich valuation (about 15.8x book value per available commentary) already prices in continued strong execution; I was not able to independently verify the share-count/dilution trend behind the very high ROE this session, which is the specific check the growth-tier rule calls for at this growth level.
recommendation_rationale: Quant composite is Hold on both windows despite genuinely exceptional growth and return metrics (quality_score ~97, growth scores ~96-98) -- this reflects the quant model's valuation and momentum inputs pulling the composite back to Hold even for a high-quality grower, which is a reasonable, not contradictory, outcome. My own research confirms the growth is real and broad-based (not a base-effect artifact), so I see no basis to second-guess the Hold, and no rule permits me to override a quant Hold to Sell in any case.
summary: Jeena Sikho Lifecare runs a fast-growing chain of Ayurvedic hospitals and clinics across India, and its most recent full year showed very strong growth in both revenue and profit as the network of centres expanded, with excellent returns on capital. The company continues to open new centres and launch new products. The stock is not cheaply priced relative to its book value, reflecting how much the market already likes this growth story. We rate it a Hold: a genuine, broad-based growth story already reflected in a rich valuation.
positive_para: Growth is real and geographically diversified across 119 centres in 23 states, not a one- or two-location fluke, with FY26 revenue up 71% and profit up 178% alongside improving working-capital metrics (debtor days down from 49 to 32) -- a sign of genuine operating quality alongside the growth, not just top-line expansion. Return ratios (ROCE 64.1%, ROE 61.3%) are exceptional even by high-growth-healthcare standards, and continued network expansion (new hospital planned for October 2026, new client-support infrastructure, new product launches) suggests the growth pipeline remains active rather than already spent.
negative_para: Growth at this magnitude (70%+ revenue, nearly 180% profit) cannot mechanically continue as the base of 119 centres scales further -- new-centre ramp-up economics typically mean each incremental centre contributes a smaller percentage lift to an ever-larger base, so a deceleration from the trailing rate should be expected and planned for rather than extrapolated. The stock's rich valuation on a book-value basis (around 15.8x) already assumes continued strong execution, and I could not independently verify the share-count/dilution trend behind the very high ROE this session, which is the specific check called for at this growth level.
reverse_dcf_judgment: ROE of 61.3% comfortably clears the 20% threshold associated with the exceptional-growth tier, and the business model (asset-light-ish healthcare-services rollout funded partly by improving working capital rather than heavy new equity) does not show obvious signs of dilution-funded growth from what is available, though I was unable to independently confirm the multi-year share-count trend this session -- that check should be completed before treating the ROE/growth combination as fully verified. Provisionally, this looks like a genuine high-quality compounder rather than a growth-by-dilution story, but the valuation already assumes the growth continues at a strong, if inevitably decelerating, pace.

technical_commentary: DATA NOTE: raw Close/Adj Close both show an apparent -80% one-month collapse in Jun-2025 (Rs2,132 to Rs426) that is in fact an un-adjusted ~1:5 stock split (confirmed via the single-day price ratio and volume jump on 2025-06-03) -- neither price column in this dataset back-adjusts for it, so all levels/MAs here are computed on a manually split-corrected series. On that corrected basis the stock rallied roughly 47x from listing (2022) to an all-time high near Rs850 (Sep-2025), and has since corrected 32% over ten months to Rs578, sitting just below its 10-month MA while the 20- and 40-month MAs remain bullish -- a real, extended, still-unresolved correction within a very strong uptrend.
